disease_label_per_paper: Pleural cavity cytokine release syndrome in CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor-modified T cell therapy
presentation_summary: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated with CD19-directed CAR-T cells after lymphodepleting fludarabine/cyclophosphamide.
Fever to 39.3 C developed the day after infusion with CRP above 100 mg/L and negative blood cultures.
Progressive cough and bilateral pleural effusion developed; pleural fluid IL-6 and CAR construct copies were markedly higher than paired blood measurements.
Symptoms attenuated by day 9, effusions resolved by day 21, and PET/CT at 1 month showed complete remission.

risk_context.source_text_value: infused with a total of 2.45 x 10^8 CART19 cells
posterior mediastinal mass and later bilateral pleural effusion after CART19 infusion
Multiple blood cultures were negative, which eliminated bacterial infection in the paper's interpretation

observations.source_text_value: progressive cough and suspected pleural effusion three days after fever began

observations.quality_note: Lower bound encoded because the paper reported CRP beyond 100 mg/L.

observations.source_text_value: CT scan showed bilateral pleural effusion; ultrasound widths 5-6 cm left and 6-7 cm right
localized pleural cavity cytokine release with bilateral effusions
paired peripheral blood serum IL-6 5.69 pg/mL when hydrothorax IL-6 was 1212.45 pg/mL
observations.quality_note: Peripheral serum IL-6 was low at the time of pleural fluid sampling despite local pleural CRS.

observations.source_text_value: progressive cough and positional symptoms from pleural effusion without reported serious hypoxemia

clinical_timeline.event: Fever 39.3 C; CRP beyond 100 mg/L; blood cultures negative; serum cytokines including IFN-gamma, IL-6 and IL-10 elevated according to the paper.
Progressive cough, especially lying down; CT and ultrasound showed bilateral pleural effusion; thoracentesis performed.
Symptoms and signs attenuated; blood test almost normal and left effusion largely absorbed.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Pleural fluid IL-6 much higher than peripheral serum
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: IL-6 at 1212.45 pg/mL in hydrothorax versus 5.69 pg/mL in blood

confirmatory_findings.finding: CAR construct copies enriched in pleural fluid compared with blood
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: qPCR CAR constructs 1119696 copies/ug DNA in hydrothorax versus 522227 copies/ug DNA in blood
suggesting a grade 2 cytokine release syndrome

actual_treatment: monitoring of cytokines and CAR construct copies

outcome.radiographic: Pleural effusion fully absorbed by day 21.
outcome.oncologic: Complete remission on PET/CT at 1 month.

quality_warnings: Pleural fluid IL-6 and local CAR qPCR are confirmatory/local-compartment evidence and marked use_in_ranking:false.
Peripheral serum IL-6 was encoded separately because the disease axis is serum_il6.
No oxygen saturation, blood pressure, or exact antimicrobial regimen was reported and none was invented.
